reference_materials: Existing Bürkle 4208-0022 and Rubbermaid 1997206 source-ledger reconstructions
findings: The current 29 captured views include 11 byte-identical images retained from the previous visual review. All new or changed views were visually inspected, including the final central-groove routing and five complete-tool positions.

The tie detail exposes a tapered rounded molded head, real feed opening, integral pawl, thin strap and internal serrations. The full stock view is a flattened inspection pose; the photographed bent tip is not a qualified free-rest shape.

The two sensor coils are separately retained above the U30 exclusion zone, below the guy collar, with their own top and bottom ties. The complete support geometry remains source-preserving under the recorded 30 degree rotation.
The black temperature adapter and separate wind adapter each have two independent ordinary ties. Heights are staggered to avoid the actual RS3 clamp, housing and bracket.
The bottom RS3 view exposes the continuous lead through the bracket hole and two ties securing it along the inclined arm. The actual mesh clearance and enclosure checks complement this visual review.

The hidden-door view exposes two real plugs in distinct logger jacks and network leads through central grooves 4 and 5. The separately sleeved grounding lead passes through groove 3; all three outside leads retain explicit drip geometry.
Detail views deliberately clip the observation bounds, exposing open display sections. Those cuts are viewer-only and are not new physical part boundaries.

The isolated grounding accessory exposes its real flag-contact mouth, conductor, black gland sleeve and ring opening. Its catalog dimensions constrain an explicit OEM-unknown hypothesis, rather than identify a factory Onset SKU.

The installed ring appears between the shifted lower-left nut and existing washer. The narrow clip window intentionally exposes display sections of neighbouring hardware; the checked physical meshes remain whole.
The cart view contains two ordinary trays. Fourteen stock-derived tapered cutoff tails and three original plugs have visible separate locations; the top view and actual-floor ray checks agree.

Five complete ordinary-tool views retain their handles, shafts and sockets in the installed context. Full-station checks separately cover enclosure states and conservative tool clearance regions. The previous wind-groove interference remains a negative example.
geometry_limits: Head opening, pawl, serration detail and bent strap shapes are authored inferences; exact manufacturing tolerances and force behavior remain unknown.
The source-specific 300 mm stock length differs from the linked family drawings nominal 305 mm. Both length and bundle discrepancies are retained.

Fourteen source-length ties account for 2.656489798724572 m retained and 1.543510201275428 m cutoffs. Physical final-state storage now exists for every cutoff and the three removed plugs. This does not establish a cutting or cleanup operation.

Whole-hand/body access, other operating interfaces, main-scene inventory and source-to-physics material/contact behavior remain incomplete. The cart reuses the existing utility_cart identity; two additional trays remain unallocated candidates.
No retention, preload, gravity settling, ratchet, electrical, weatherproofing or robot-execution qualification follows from these images.

The selected 400 mm grounding length, conductor radius, local crimp/housing details and colors remain inferred. Tool-space regions retain rigid flexible leads and do not validate a robot trajectory, electrical bond, seal or torque.
